perspective:
Christian’s available information:

- He is a police officer and has been childhood friends with Jonathan. He often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his perspective.
- He had been feeling that Jonathan was hiding something important. This made him anxious and suspicious.
- He arranged and attended a meeting with Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop to confront him.
- In that meeting, Christian told Jonathan he felt Jonathan was hiding something. He heard Jonathan say Christian could trust him.
- Christian said Jonathan had been acting differently and asked what was going on. He heard Jonathan admit that he had been keeping something: Jonathan said he was in some trouble and did not know how to tell him.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic. He offered to help and said they could face it together. He heard Jonathan say the situation was complicated, that he didn’t want to drag Christian into it, but that he could use support and resources to get out of the mess.
- Christian began to believe Jonathan’s trouble might be related to criminal activity. He felt conflicted and concerned but decided to investigate discreetly without alarming Jonathan.
- Christian asked Jonathan whether the trouble was related to anything illegal. He heard Jonathan say he couldn’t say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he did not do anything illegal himself.
- Christian said he would look into it discreetly to make sure Jonathan was safe. He heard Jonathan thank him and say he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Through his own investigation, Christian came to believe/claim that Jonathan was being framed and that someone was trying to set him up. He felt determined and protective and decided to clear Jonathan’s name by gathering evidence.
- Christian told Jonathan he believed Jonathan was being framed. He heard Jonathan ask if he was sure and who would do such a thing.
- Christian said he was not sure yet but had leads and would gather more evidence. He heard Jonathan thank him and say he didn’t know what he would do without him.
- Christian later came to believe/claim that he had found out who was behind it: someone both he and Jonathan knew and trusted. He felt betrayed and resolute.
- Christian told Jonathan this and said he would confront the person and bring them to justice. He heard Jonathan warn him to be careful, say the person was dangerous, and say he trusted Christian to do what was right.
- Christian says he knows the specific identity of the culprit, though the provided dialogue does not reveal that name.
- Christian has not heard Jonathan admit to any actual illegal act; Jonathan only denied doing anything illegal himself and mentioned possibly being involved with the wrong people.
